Rashi on Shabbat 119b:10:1.english: My anointed ones, these are the schoolchildren - For it is the custom [with] young children to anoint them with oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:10:2.hebrew: ובנביאי אלו תלמידי חכמים - שנאמר, "ונביא לבב חכמה" (תהילים צ׳:י״ב):
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:10:2.english: And My prophets — these are Torah scholars - As it is stated: "And we shall gain a heart of wisdom" (Psalms 90:12).

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:10:3.english: They destroy [it] - There is a remnant.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:10:4.english: They devote [it] to destruction - there is no remnant.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:11:1.hebrew: מתכסין בהן כשמלה - כששואלין אותן טעמי תורה, הללו עושין עצמן כמעלימין את דבריהם, מפני שאינן יודעים להשיב:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:11:1.english: [They] cover themselves with them like a garment - When people ask them [for] reasons of Torah, these [people] act as though concealing their words, because they do not know [how] to answer.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:11:2.hebrew: ישנן בידך - אתה בקי, לפיכך קצין תהיה לנו ותלמדנו חכמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:11:2.english: [They] are in your hands - You are well-versed [in them]; therefore, you shall be a chief over us and teach us wisdom.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:1:1.hebrew: מהדר אזוזי זוזי דרבנן - כשהיה רואה אותן זוגות זוגות ומדברין בתורה, מחזר אחריהם ואומר להם: במטותא מנכון, לכו והתעסקו בעונג שבת, ולא תחללוניה לבטל תענוגים:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:1:1.english: He would go around to pairs of Sages - When he would see them in pairs, conversing in Torah, he would seek them out and say to them: "Please, go and engage in the delight of Shabbat, and do not desecrate it by neglecting [its] pleasures."

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:2:1.english: They finished [vaykhallu] - [That is,] the Holy One, Blessed be He, and this [person] who recounts the praise of the Omnipresent and the praise of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:1.hebrew: יסדר אדם שלחנו בע"ש - ללילי שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:1.english: A person should set his table on Shabbat eve - For Shabbat night.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:2.hebrew: במוצ"ש - נמי כבוד שבת, ללוות ביציאתו דרך כבוד, כאדם המלוה את המלך בצאתו מן העיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:2.english: At the conclusion of Shabbat - [This is] also honoring Shabbat, to escort it upon its departure in an honorable manner, like a person who escorts the king when he leaves the city.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:3.english: Hot water - To drink and to bathe.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:4:5.english: A lion ate it - [referring] to the calf that was fit to be slaughtered.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:1.english: With all his might - With all his intent.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:2.hebrew: בפרוע פרעות - ביטול פורעניות, כגון פרוע דמתרגמין בטל:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:2.english: When punishments are annulled - [This means] the annulment of punishments, like [the word] paru'a, which we translate [into Aramaic as] batel [annulled].

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:3.english: When the people offer themselves, bless - When Israel volunteers to bless their Creator.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:4.hebrew: כי פרוע - כי פרעו אהרן ע"ז. והכי קאמר: בהבטל פריעות ע"ז שתשתקע ותשתכח שלא יזכר עונם, משום התנדב עם הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:4.english: That [the nation] was wild [paru’a] - For Aaron let them loose [into] idolatry. And this is what [the verse] is saying: when the wildness of idolatry is annulled, so that it sinks and is forgotten [and] their sin is not remembered, it is because of “[when] the people offer themselves” [to bless God].

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:5:5.english: God, faithful King - Thus [he] testifies about his Creator that He is God, faithful King.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:6:1.english: When people are not found to extinguish it - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:7:1.hebrew: בבקר - בזמן ק"ש, וכן מאחרי בנשף:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:7:1.english: In the morning - At the time of [the] recitation of Shema, and similarly [with] "those who tarry into the evening" [at the time of the evening Shema].

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:7:2.hebrew: והיה כנור ונבל - בסיפיה דקרא, "ואת פועל ה' לא יביטו" — לא שמו לב ליחד שמו על בריותיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:7:2.english: And [there] shall be lyre and lute - At the end of the verse, [it states,] "and they do not look upon the work of God" — they did not pay attention to unify His name over His creations.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:8:1.hebrew: שפוך על עולל - רישא דקרא: "ואת חמת ה' נלאיתי הכיל שפוך וגו'" — שפוך החמה בנקמה, בשביל שעולל לחוץ ובטלין מבית רבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:8:1.english: Pour [it] upon the infant - The beginning of the verse [is]: "And the wrath of God I am weary of containing, pour [it], etc." — pour out the wrath in vengeance, because the infant is outside and they are idle from the schoolhouse.

Rashi on Shabbat 119b:8:2.hebrew: הובישו כי תועבה עשו וגו' - סיפיה דקרא, גם בוש לא יבושו וגם הכלם לא כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 119b:8:2.english: They acted shamefully, for they have performed abominations, etc. - The end of the verse [reads]: "yet they neither were ashamed, nor [did they know] humiliation," etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:1:1.hebrew: א"ר חנינא אל מלך נאמן - צריך להרהר בו בשעה שאומר אמן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:1:1.english: Rabbi Chanina said: "God, faithful King" (El Melekh Ne'eman) - One must meditate upon it at the time one says "Amen."

Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:3:1.hebrew: ומצא נר דלוק ושולחן ערוך - וא"ת, דאמר בריש ערבי פסחים (פסחים דף ק:): "ושוין שאין מביאין את השולחן אא"כ קידש"? וי"ל, דערוך הוא במקום אחר, אלא שאין מביאין אותו עד אחר הקידוש, כי היכי דתיתי סעודתא ביקרא דשבת, כדאיתא בשאלתות דרב אחאי. ודוקא בימיהם, שהיו להם שלחנות קטנים לפני כל אחד ואחד, אבל שלנו גדולים הם וקשה לטלטלם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:3:1.english: And [he] finds a lamp burning and a table set - And if you ask: For it states at the beginning of [the chapter] Arvei Pesaḥim (Pesaḥim 100b): "And they agree that one does not bring in the table unless one has recited Kiddush"? One can answer that it is [already] set in another place, except that they do not bring it in until after Kiddush, so that the meal comes in honor of Shabbat, as it is stated in the She'iltot of Rav Aḥai. And [this] applies specifically in their days, when they had small tables before each and every person, whereas ours are large and it is difficult to move them.

Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:5:1.hebrew: כל העונה אמן יהא שמיה רבא בכל כחו - פי' בכל כוונתו, וכן פירש רש"י. ור"י אומר דיש בפסיקתא במעשה דר' ישמעאל בן אלישע, דקאמר התם: כשישראל נכנסים לבתי כנסיות ואומרים "יהא שמיה רבא מברך" בקול רם — מבטלים גזירות קשות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:5:1.english: Anyone who answers "Amen, may His great name be blessed" with all his might - [This] means with all his concentration, and so Rashi explained. And Ri says that there is [a passage] in the Pesikta in the story of Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, where it says there: When Israel enters the synagogues and says "May His great name be blessed" in a loud voice, they annul harsh decrees.

Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:5:2.hebrew: א"ר חנינא אל מלך נאמן - צריך להרהר בו בשעה שאומר אמן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 119b:5:2.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said: "God, faithful King [El Melekh ne'eman]" - One must contemplate it at the time he says amen.
